title: E and I
summary: Two vowels, one row up — and suddenly most of what you can type is real English.
intro: E is the most common letter in English and I is not far behind, so these two reaches will end up being among the most worn-in movements you own. Both are upward, with the middle fingers, from D and K. As before: reach, press, return. Adding these two keys roughly triples how much English you can write, which you will notice within a screen or two.
congrats: That is the moment the course stops feeling like exercises. With E and I you can write hundreds of real words, and from here every lesson is mostly reading and typing rather than drilling.

screens.text: Left middle finger, up and slightly left from D. The most common letter in the language — this reach is worth getting exactly right.
E then D, up and back. The finger should return far enough to feel D under it again.
screens.content:
des des
dsf kej ds
se es sese

screens.text: Right middle finger, up from K. Same movement mirrored, and the last of the four reaches this unit teaches.
I then K. If your whole hand lifts, the reach is too big — only the finger needs to travel.
screens.content:
ilk kil
jlk dif jl
li il lili

screens.text: Words already, rather than letter patterns. That is what two vowels buy you.
Both new keys in real words. Read each word whole; your fingers can handle the spelling.
screens.content:

flakes as lash glass
shake shades if sales

screens.text: Weighted towards I. It appears in more English words than any consonant.
screens.content:

fails said saga alfalfa

screens.text: A longer burst. If you make a mistake, keep going — stopping to feel bad about it costs more than the mistake did.
One pattern screen to check the return. Middle fingers up and back, index fingers never moving.

screens.text: Longer lines now that there are enough words to fill them. Keep an even pace across the whole line.
